hints.content:
This is the process for determining the sine or cosine of any angle $\theta$:

1. Starting from the point $(1,0)$, move counterclockwise along the unit circle until the angle that is formed between your position, the origin, and the positive $x$-axis is equal to $\theta$.
2. The $x$-coordinate of that point is equal to $\cos(\theta)$ and the $y$-coordinate of that point is equal to $\sin(\theta)$.

According to this the definition, which point corresponds to an angle of $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ (in radians)?

Point $B$ corresponds to an angle of $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.

[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore, its $x$-coordinate will give us $\cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)$.

options.alt: A unit circle on an x y coordinate plane where the center of the unit circle is at the origin and the circumference of the circle touches (one, zero), (zero, one), (negative one, zero), and (zero, negative one). Point A is located at near twelve thirty o'clock on the circle. Point B is located near ten thirty o'clock on the circle. Point C is located near six o'clock on the circle. A line segment extends from (zero, zero) to point B. An angle from the arc starting at (one, zero) and opening counter clockwise to point B has an angle measurement of three pi over four radians.

hints.content: In conclusion, the coordinate that is equal to $\cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)$ is the $x$-coordinate of point $B$.
